what_this_is: Source-to-destination reconciliation of every import unit, from a combined load of the real private artifacts into an isolated, disposable local database built from the full migration union. Counts, digests and statuses only. Not a hosted load: nothing here was written to a hosted project.
rights_note: Loading changes nothing about rights: every rights row is pending and link-only. A loaded row is not a published row.

tested_source.note: The receipts pin the commit of the checkout that produced them. This manifest is evidence about that commit only; a later commit that changes source code is not covered by it.

totals.populations_note: Counters are per population (ledger records, statistical observations, catalogue entry versions). They are never added across populations.

count_invariants.rule: per unit and population: inserted <= seen, and inserted + unchanged + rejected + conflicts = seen

order_independence.compared: the same artifacts loaded into a second fresh database in the opposite family order
order_independence.how: per data table: the row count, and a digest of every row's content after the stated normalisation (content_digest.ts). Equal digests mean equal content, not only equal counts.

normalisation.method: row digests refined in rounds: each round replaces every reference with the digest the referred row had in the round before, so cycles converge and no surrogate id is ever compared
normalisation.refinement_note: complete means the last round told no more rows apart than the one before, so no further round could change what is compared
normalisation.references: replaced by the content of the row referred to; a declared foreign key names its table, an undeclared uuid column is resolved only by verifying that every one of its values is an id of that table
normalisation.database_clock_columns: left out (a default of now()): they record when a load ran, not what was loaded
normalisation.run_ledger: references to run-ledger tables are left out, and those tables are counted but never compared
normalisation.everything_else: every other column of every row is inside the digest (its JSON text), so equal digests mean equal content
